cases.input: R1 pins P v2.1, A@s41, B@s17 and code c9; R2 pins A@s42, B@s17 and the same definition.
cases.expect: Runs, input states, outputs and lineage assertions remain independently addressable.

cases.input: R2 task attempt 1 fails and attempt 2 succeeds under one start-pinned manifest.
cases.expect: Both attempts remain immutable children of R2; the retry neither replaces the manifest nor mints a new run.

cases.input: A WM-XCT-012 Activity changes D@v8 into distinct snapshot D@v9 with actor, time, ticket/patch evidence and a WM-DAT-006 context fragment.
cases.expect: The activity and propagated manual dependency are recorded without inventing a pipeline run, manifest aggregate or mutation of D@v8.

cases.input: Vendor input C has no accessible upstream lineage.
cases.expect: C remains a boundary node with unresolved ancestry and reduced confidence.

cases.input: Two columns with the same name are asserted as directly derived without evidence.
cases.expect: The direct edge is rejected; name matching may only be low-confidence inferred evidence.

cases.input: No stored edge is interpreted as proof that no dependency exists.
cases.expect: The inference is rejected outside an explicit closed-world perimeter.

cases.input: A successful run is treated as proof that its output passed quality and publication gates.
cases.expect: The inference is rejected because execution, quality, publication and acceptance are separate assertions.

cases.input: Two pipelines reuse the same SQL digest and therefore treat it as a Transformation aggregate.
cases.expect: The aggregate inference is rejected; shared content-addressed payload is not mastership.

cases.input: Failed attempt A1 leaves a durable partial output before A2 succeeds.
cases.expect: The partial output has its own external snapshot identity and assertions; it is not silently merged into A2.

cases.input: A lineage assertion has endpoints but no producing task, attempt or evidenced activity.
cases.expect: The assertion is rejected as orphaned even though its record would otherwise be addressable.
